adrs.decisionSummary: 1. All Sprint 11 agents share a **single frontier chat-completion deployment** in the `westus2` demo Foundry project per ADR-0013 (demo scope only). The deployment name is referenced by each agent manifest as `modelDeploymentRef: sprint11-chat` — the concrete Azure deployment name is resolved at Sprint 13 agent-host configuration time and is **not** hard-coded in any prompt, manifest, or workflow. 2. This deployment is **synthetic-data-only**. Per ADR-0006 and ADR-0016 it is **non-production for regulated data** and must never process real PHI. Enforcement is layered: agent refusal rules (per-agent `AGENT.md`), the synthetic-only Sprint 10 Gold tables, and the `data-quality-agent` PHI gate. 3. Every Sprint 11 agent `AGENT.md` **references this ADR** in its Identity or Grounding section so that the model-selection decision is traceable from the agent to the constraint set above. 4. When the platform sunsets ADR-0013 and returns to Switzerland North, this ADR is **superseded** by a new ADR that pins Swiss-resident deployments per agent and lifts the synthetic-only restriction for regulated data.
adrs.title: Sprint 11 agent model selection

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: The solution shall provide a copilot interface for operations teams to query bed and flow status.

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: The copilot shall provide grounded answers based on live operational data, forecast outputs, and discharge signals.

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: The copilot shall provide bottleneck explanations and recommended operational options.

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: The copilot shall present current bed state, predicted pressure windows, and likely same-day discharges.

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: Power BI-based operational visibility shall be available for non-conversational usage scenarios.

requirements.family: Bed Management Copilot And User Experience
requirements.title: Copilot responses shall preserve references to source context and response timestamp metadata.
The platform shall ingest provider-internal operational signals, including ED, ADT, bed-state, and discharge-related events.
The platform shall support HL7 FHIR-oriented normalization where healthcare interoperability requires it.
The platform shall maintain curated datasets that unify operational, planning, and model input data.
The platform shall capture partner acknowledgements and status updates from integration flows.
The platform shall expose governed semantic models for dashboard and copilot consumption.
The platform shall support data ingestion from KIS/EHR, ED systems, bed management systems, and staffing/planning systems.
The platform shall support outbound and inbound orchestration with downstream partners via integration workflows.
The platform shall keep source-to-consumption traceability for operational and AI-serving datasets.
The solution shall identify inpatients approaching discharge readiness.
The solution shall produce ranked discharge candidates with explanatory factors.
The solution shall trigger integration-based downstream actions for discharge coordination.
The solution shall record outbound coordination events and returned partner statuses.
The solution shall surface discharge blockers to operations users.
The solution shall make discharge-readiness outputs available to dashboards and copilot interactions.
The solution shall produce a 72-hour demand forecast for emergency demand and admission pressure.
Forecast outputs shall be segmented by specialty and time window.
Forecasting shall use provider-internal arrivals plus downstream capacity signals as model inputs.
Forecast outputs shall be published to operations-facing dashboards.
Forecast outputs shall be available as grounding context for the bed management copilot.
Forecast generation runs shall persist execution timestamps and model run identifiers for auditability.
The solution shall provide auditable traceability between source data, model outputs, user-facing answers, and integration events.
The solution shall support access-control enforcement for clinical and operational data surfaces.
The delivery model shall support structured promotion across DEV, SIT, and PROD stages.
The solution shall produce governance evidence artifacts for compliance reviews.
The solution shall support policy-driven integration controls for outbound partner interactions.
The solution shall maintain provider-local control over prompts, model configuration, and operational workflows.
The data-governance RACI shall include a nominated **semantic / ontology owner**. Documented in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) as of v1.4.0.

Ontology changes shall follow an **OBO-inspired semantic change workflow** (proposal → domain-owner review → versioned release → downstream impact check), mirroring the data-contract breaking-change control in `NFR-MAINT-002`.

The delivery pipeline shall include a **CI conformance check** verifying that every operational-layer entity maps to a reference-layer class (or is explicitly annotated as reference-layer-exempt). Failure fails the build.
The solution shall be deployed for one hospital provider instance at a time.
The solution shall support provider-internal governance and data ownership boundaries.
The solution shall support an implementation sequence for USZ-first or LUKS-first rollout patterns.
External care entities shall be integrated as endpoints and not as first-class platform operators.
The product shall support a phased implementation model where capabilities can be enabled incrementally.
The platform shall onboard new patients using a minimum required metadata set only.
The platform shall onboard hospital capacity using specialty-tagged metadata.
The platform shall support provider-specific specialty profiles for capacity planning.
The platform shall classify onboarding workflows as deterministic service vs agentic flow using a documented criterion.

The platform shall maintain a **reference ontology** authored in OWL/RDF, importing established published ontologies (BFO ISO/IEC 21838-2:2021, OMRSE, OGMS, OOSTT, Goyer et al. healthcare-system classes) and adding the platform-specific `CapacityUnit` abstraction with subtypes for bed, OR slot, room, staff shift and device.

The platform shall realise the **operational ontology** in Fabric IQ, auto-generated from the governed semantic model with static (lakehouse) and time-series (eventhouse) bindings. Use in `switzerlandnorth` PROD paths carrying PHI is gated on Fabric IQ Switzerland-region GA + DPA equivalence per ADR-0014 gate G-C; use in the `westus2` demo scope is permitted per ADR-0013.

The platform shall model all in-scope hospital resource dimensions (beds, OR slots, rooms, staff shifts, devices) as **capacity-unit subtypes** with shared states (available / occupied / blocked / planned) and shared relations, so one set of KPIs, forecasts and simulation logic applies across all dimensions.
The copilot and Fabric Data Agents shall **ground responses on ontology entities and relationships** to deliver concept-level traceability, extending `NFR-AI-002/003/004`.
The platform shall provide a **process-ontology overlay** on the reference layer to support what-if simulation (`FR-SIM-*` when introduced).
The ontology shall carry a **crosswalk to FHIR resource types and SNOMED CT concepts** for clinical interoperability (extends `FR-DATA-002`).
The ontology shall support **provider-specific extensions** (specialisations) without re-architecture, realising `NFR-MAINT-004` at the semantic layer.
The platform shall provide an operational **bed-capacity dashboard page** exposing current occupancy, forecast pressure windows, and data-quality signals, aligned with `FR-CX-005`.

The platform shall provide an operational **OR-steering dashboard page** exposing case-level utilisation, first-case on-time performance, cancellation, and idle-slot metrics, aligned with `FR-CX-005`.
Copilot outputs shall remain advisory and shall not replace human operational authority.
Copilot outputs shall be retrieval-grounded in provider operational context and model outputs.
Forecast and discharge model outputs shall be traceable to model version and execution time.
User-facing AI responses and coordination triggers shall be auditable to source context.
AI-serving behavior shall support provider-local governance and change control.
The solution shall support Swiss DSG compliance for healthcare data handling.
The solution shall support cantonal healthcare governance requirements in deployment and operations controls.
The solution shall support KVG/LAMal-aligned operational governance where applicable to patient flow data usage.
Data residency controls shall support Switzerland or permitted jurisdiction constraints for each dataset class.
The solution shall maintain a data processing inventory with legal basis and purpose tags for PHI and operational datasets.
The solution shall provide a documented data-subject-rights operating process with accountable ownership and response SLAs.
The solution shall implement policy-enforced default-deny behavior for PHI cross-border transfer and failover activation unless explicitly approved.
The solution shall maintain auditable privacy incident handling and notification decision workflows.
If EPR integration is enabled, the solution shall enforce consent, identity, access, and logging controls aligned to EPDG/EPDV-EDI obligations.
The solution shall maintain compliance evidence artifacts and review cadence mapped to legal obligations and internal controls.
Onboarding data contracts shall enforce minimum-sensitive-data controls and purpose tags (Sprint 6).
Critical operational feeds shall include quality checks for completeness and schema validity.
Curated operational datasets shall support lineage from source to serving views.
Data model changes shall preserve backward compatibility or include controlled migration plans.
Integration message failures shall be observable and recoverable without silent data loss.
Specialty metadata shall include quality checks and controlled versioning (Sprint 6).
The platform shall record change-management traceability for semantic-model, dashboard, and agent artefacts (aligns with `FR-GOV-001`).
The platform shall support audit-review workflows for governance evidence artefacts (aligns with `FR-GOV-004`).
The dashboard consumption path shall enforce role-scoped filtering that prevents PHI-tagged column exposure to any non-owner role (extends [ADR-0016](adr/0016-no-phi-in-mvp-demo-scope.md) gate 4).
Semantic-model and dashboard artefacts shall be round-trippable to source-controlled TMDL/PBIP such that any deployed state can be replayed from repository content alone.
Governance evidence artefacts shall be co-located with the sprint or ADR that produced them under `docs/sprints/*/evidence/` or `docs/adr/*.md`.

Every dashboard visual shall carry per-visual traceability back to its underlying semantic-model measure and its ontology-grounded source (`hcp:*` entities), aligned with `FR-CX-006` and `FR-ONT-004`.
The solution shall support modular architecture lanes for data, AI, app, integration, and governance assets.
Delivery workflows shall be Git-first and support auditable promotion across environments.
Requirement artifacts shall remain traceable to specification sources and implementation increments.
Platform configuration shall support provider-specific rollout without full re-architecture.
Sprint 6 onboarding and MVP agent services shall be deployable through IaC-first pipelines with reproducible environment bootstrap (Sprint 6).

The ontology (reference layer OWL/RDF + operational layer Fabric IQ + crosswalk) shall be **versioned, governed and promoted as a first-class asset** with DEV/SIT/PROD gates, an explicit reference↔operational crosswalk artefact (`docs/ontology/crosswalk.md`), and a **CI conformance check** enforcing `FR-GOV-ONT-003`. Extends `NFR-MAINT-002`.
Ingestion shall support near-real-time updates for ED, ADT, bed-state, and discharge status signals.
Forecast inference shall support at least hourly refresh cadence for the 72-hour horizon.
Discharge-readiness scoring shall support multiple recalculations per day.
The platform shall support burst headroom above average event volume.
End-user operational surfaces shall support interactive decision cycles without batch-only dependence.
The platform shall support continuous operations and shall not be designed as overnight batch-only service.
Critical data and inference pipelines shall provide failure visibility and restartability.
Operational dashboards and copilot services shall degrade gracefully when non-critical dependencies fail.
Integration workflows shall provide retry and exception-handling behavior for transient endpoint errors.
Onboarding services shall remain available under defined degraded-mode behavior (Sprint 6).
Access shall be least-privilege and role-scoped by user and service identity.
Data access attempts and privilege changes shall be fully auditable.
Integration endpoints shall enforce authenticated and authorized communication patterns.
Secret material shall be managed outside source-controlled artifacts.
Onboarding identity and cross-tenant boundaries shall be explicit and auditable (Sprint 6).
